runner: Azure ACR task, software WebGL2 (SwiftShader), 640x360, dpr 1; spec tests/browser/bloom-fusion-variants.spec.ts
scene: PBR viewer (milk truck, HDRI, shadowed sun, cinematic-tier bloom, ACES), rebuilt against the in-repo sources
decisionRule: no software-GL frame-time regression against production (<= +5%) and draws <= 25
regression: The first fusion (2-D blur for mips 1-4) cost 633 ms against 407 ms on the candidate bench: 11.1M texel fetches against 1.1M for the separable pairs, on a software rasteriser.

round1_5frames_x2reps.note: + bright extract folded into the level-0 downsample

chosenDefault.note: 2-D blur only for the two smallest mips (1.3M + 0.5M texel fetches). Draws 25. Frame time -7.1% (confirmation) and about -2% in a second batch on a busier runner; never above production.

whyItIsFaster: The bright extract (a full-resolution pass) is folded into the level-0 downsample, and the full-resolution upsample is folded into the composite, so two 640x360 passes disappear; that fill outweighs the 2-D blur on the two smallest mips.
lookNeutral: auto vs production, same frame: mean abs diff 0.001/255, max 1/255.
persistGlStateFinding: Removed (2026-10-28). Keeping the GL state shadow across frames did not move frame time or CPU, and an adversarial review found its root cause of divergence: the sampler registry kept a second shadow (active unit, per-unit texture bindings) that stateCache.invalidate() did not clear, and the presentation snapshot restored only units 0-2 while the fused mip sum binds 0-4. Both are now fixed regardless: stateCache.invalidate() resets every registered dependent shadow (the sampler registry registers itself), and the snapshot saves and restores units 0-4. Guard: tests/unit/rendering/post-chain-texture-unit-shadow.test.ts.
showcaseGame_heatsink: auto vs production, 3 stepped frames (settle(30) then step), Math.random seeded, HDRI settled: mean 0.001/255, max 1/255, 0 pixels over 6/255 on every frame (runs p1-shadow-c and p1-shadow-d). The production-vs-production control was 0 in one run and 14-16/255 in the other: the route is not fully deterministic across loads, so the auto row is the meaningful one. Every fusion variant (off, acc only, ext only, b2d3 only, default) was also within 0.001/255. An earlier failing run (mean 13-24/255) captured before the HDRI chain finished; the spec now waits for hdriStatus to leave pending.
